content: Suppose xs : List A. What is the best way to refer to the function Nat -> Option A which is given by getElem?, i.e. (xs[·]?)? Why do we define List.get but not List.get? I ask because I want to use this as a monadic function, rather than focusing on individual elements.
If you really desire for a name, then List.get?Internal would be that function. I'm confused as to why you need to explicitly name (xs[.]?)
As I say, it arose naturally in some work I was doing, because it's a monadic map into the Option monad.

When my cursor hovers over an expression (xs[i]?) in the online web editor, part of the resulting message says that " ... the recommended spelling of xs[i]? in identifiers is getElem?". Searching for getElem? in the api docs shows that it's a method of the GetElem? typeclass. If the fact that List.get?Internal is an internal detail is undesirable, then I think you could use the GetElem?.getElem? method (or use the unqualified getElem?).
